steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on a transformer-based point cloud registration method that uses skeletal priors, aimed at cross-source data and unstructured scenes. Explain the challenges, motivate the use of skeletons, describe the method's components and the experiments, and list our contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
1. Point cloud registration and new challenges
2. Why unstructured scenes and cross-source data are hard
3. Skeletons as a geometric prior -> SPEAL
4. Components: SEM, SAGTR, CDS
5. Experiments
6. Contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. Background
- point cloud registration: essential in graphics, vision, robotics
- estimate rigid transformation aligning two partially overlapping point cloud frames
- surge of learning-based methods; progress on sparsity, partial overlap, complex distribution in large outdoor scenes
- but practical application + advances in acquisition -> new challenges: unstructured scenes, cross-source data

2. Challenges
- unstructured scenes: complex natural scenes/objects -> hard to learn discriminative features -> degraded registration
- cross-source: partial overlap + large differences in scale and density -> hard feature matching
- noise + outliers from different sources -> worse correspondences
- existing methods: only same-source, or ignore intrinsic topological natures -> suboptimal in cross-source and unstructured scenes

3. Skeletons + SPEAL
- skeletons: efficient, robust geometric representation; potential in point cloud understanding tasks; encode geometric intricacy
- SPEAL (Skeletal Prior Embedded Attention Learning), transformer-based
- skeletal geometric priors -> discriminative features -> accurate, robust correspondences
- first to use skeletal geometric priors for registration
- priors explicitly encode intrinsic topological characteristics (Fig. 1)

4. Components
- SEM (Skeleton Extraction Module): insights from medial axis transform (MAT); unsupervised skeleton points + skeletal features; robust to noise, density variances
- SAGTR (Skeleton-Aware GeoTRansformer): skeleton-aware discriminative features; captures topological natures; inter-point-cloud geometric correlations
- CDS (Correspondence Dual-Sampler): samples from superpoints and skeleton points -> reliable coarse correspondences aware of skeletal structure

5. Experiments
- KITTI Odometry (large-scale outdoor benchmark) + our cross-source variant KITTI CrossSource
- large-scale cross-source dataset, mostly unstructured forest scenes
- SPEAL effective, robust: same-source, cross-source, unstructured scenes

6. Contributions
- SPEAL: first to use skeletal representations as geometric prior
- SEM effective, portable; SAGTR + CDS accurate, robust correspondences
- KITTI CrossSource: answers dire need for cross-source benchmarks; bridge sensor technology and cross-source applications

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Point cloud registration is an essential task in graphics, vision and robotics. Its aim is to estimate a rigid transformation that aligns two frames of point clouds that partially overlap. Recently there has been a lot of interest in learning-based point cloud registration methods. These methods have made significant progress on the sparsity, the partial overlap and the complex distribution of point clouds in large outdoor scenes. But practical applications and advances in point cloud acquisition bring more challenges for point cloud registration, including unstructured scenes and cross-source data.

In unstructured scenes, the natural scenes and objects are complex, and this often makes it hard to learn discriminative features for registration, so registration algorithms perform worse. With cross-source data, the challenges mainly come from partial overlap and also from big differences in scale and density, which make effective feature matching difficult. On top of that, noise and outliers from different sources together make the quality of correspondences worse. Existing methods either only focus on same-source point clouds or they overlook the intrinsic topological natures of the point clouds. Because of this they get suboptimal results in challenging scenarios like cross-source point cloud registration and unstructured scenes.

We observed that skeletons are an efficient and robust geometric representation for point clouds and have significant potential in various point cloud understanding tasks. They can effectively encode the geometric intricacy of point clouds. Inspired by this, we propose a new transformer-based approach called Skeletal Prior Embedded Attention Learning (SPEAL) to address the challenges above. Our method uses skeletal geometric priors to learn discriminative features for accurate and robust correspondences. As far as we know, our approach is the first to use skeletal geometric priors to help point cloud registration. These skeletal geometric priors encourage robust feature learning because they explicitly encode the intrinsic topological characteristics, and this helps the correspondences and the registration results, as shown in Fig. 1.

- components: SEM (Skeleton Extraction Module): insights from medial axis transform (MAT), unsupervised skeleton points + skeletal features, robust to noise and density variances; SAGTR (Skeleton-Aware GeoTRansformer): skeleton-aware discriminative features, topological natures, inter-point-cloud geometric correlations; CDS (Correspondence Dual-Sampler): sample from superpoints and skeleton points -> reliable coarse correspondences
- experiments: KITTI Odometry (large-scale outdoor benchmark) + our KITTI CrossSource variant; large-scale cross-source dataset of mostly unstructured forest scenes -> SPEAL effective and robust for same-source, cross-source, unstructured scenes
- contributions: SPEAL first with skeletal representations as geometric prior; SEM effective, portable, SAGTR + CDS accurate/robust correspondences; KITTI CrossSource meets dire need for cross-source benchmarks, bridges sensor technology and cross-source applications

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Point cloud registration is an essential task in graphics, vision and robotics. Its aim is to estimate a rigid transformation that aligns two frames of point clouds that partially overlap. Recently there has been a lot of interest in learning-based point cloud registration methods. These methods have made significant progress on the sparsity, the partial overlap and the complex distribution of point clouds in large outdoor scenes. But practical applications and advances in point cloud acquisition bring more challenges for point cloud registration, including unstructured scenes and cross-source data.

In unstructured scenes, the natural scenes and objects are complex, and this often makes it hard to learn discriminative features for registration, so registration algorithms perform worse. With cross-source data, the challenges mainly come from partial overlap and also from big differences in scale and density, which make effective feature matching difficult. On top of that, noise and outliers from different sources together make the quality of correspondences worse. Existing methods either only focus on same-source point clouds or they overlook the intrinsic topological natures of the point clouds. Because of this they get suboptimal results in challenging scenarios like cross-source point cloud registration and unstructured scenes.

We observed that skeletons are an efficient and robust geometric representation for point clouds and have significant potential in various point cloud understanding tasks. They can effectively encode the geometric intricacy of point clouds. Inspired by this, we propose a new transformer-based approach called Skeletal Prior Embedded Attention Learning (SPEAL) to address the challenges above. Our method uses skeletal geometric priors to learn discriminative features for accurate and robust correspondences. As far as we know, our approach is the first to use skeletal geometric priors to help point cloud registration. These skeletal geometric priors encourage robust feature learning because they explicitly encode the intrinsic topological characteristics, and this helps the correspondences and the registration results, as shown in Fig. 1.

To incorporate skeletal representations as a geometric prior, SPEAL has three key components: Skeleton Extraction Module (SEM), Skeleton-Aware GeoTRansformer (SAGTR) and Correspondence Dual-Sampler (CDS). First, SEM takes insights from the medial axis transform (MAT) and extracts a set of skeleton points with skeletal features from the input point clouds, in an unsupervised way. SEM is robust to noise and density variances. Next, SAGTR is designed to learn skeleton-aware discriminative features, which help to get accurate and robust correspondences. It explicitly captures the topological natures and it learns inter-point-cloud geometric correlations effectively with our skeletal representations. Finally, CDS samples reliable correspondences from both superpoints and skeleton points, which gives reliable coarse correspondences that are aware of the skeletal structure.

We carry out extensive experiments on two datasets. The first one is KITTI Odometry, which is a large-scale outdoor registration benchmark, together with a cross-source variant of it that we propose, called KITTI CrossSource. The second one is a large-scale cross-source dataset that mostly consists of unstructured forest scenes. The results show that SPEAL is effective and robust for same-source and cross-source point cloud registration, and also for point clouds of unstructured scenes.

Overall, we have three contributions:

- We propose SPEAL, a new learning-based point cloud registration approach. It is the first to use skeletal representations as a geometric prior to get improved performance.

- The proposed SEM is an effective and portable skeleton extractor. Our SAGTR together with CDS produces accurate and robust correspondences for same-source and cross-source point cloud registration.

- KITTI CrossSource is a new cross-source point cloud dataset, and it meets the dire need for cross-source point cloud registration benchmarks. It opens up the possibility of bridging the gap between sensor technology and cross-source applications.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Point cloud registration is an essential task in graphics, vision, and robotics. It aims to estimate a rigid transformation that aligns two partially overlapping frames of point clouds. Recently, there has been a surge of interest in learning-based point cloud registration methods, which have made significant progress in addressing the sparsity, partial overlap, and complex distribution of point clouds in large outdoor scenes [1,2,3,4]. However, practical applications and advances in point cloud acquisition present further challenges for point cloud registration, including unstructured scenes and cross-source data.

In unstructured scenes, complex natural scenes and objects often make it difficult to learn discriminative features for registration, which degrades the performance of registration algorithms. For cross-source data, the challenges mainly arise from partial overlap as well as considerable differences in scale and density, leading to difficulties in effective feature matching. The combination of noise and outliers from different sources further downgrades the quality of correspondences. Existing methods either focus solely on same-source point clouds or overlook the intrinsic topological natures of the point clouds, which leads to suboptimal results in challenging scenarios such as cross-source point cloud registration and unstructured scenes.

We have observed that skeletons serve as an efficient and robust geometric representation for point clouds, showing significant potential in various point cloud understanding tasks [5,6], and can effectively encode the geometric intricacy of point clouds. Inspired by this, we propose a novel transformer-based approach, termed Skeletal Prior Embedded Attention Learning (SPEAL), to address the challenges above. Our method utilizes skeletal geometric priors to learn discriminative features for accurate and robust correspondences. To the best of our knowledge, our approach is the first to facilitate point cloud registration with skeletal geometric priors. Such priors encourage robust feature learning by explicitly encoding the intrinsic topological characteristics, which facilitates the correspondences and registration results, as shown in Fig. 1.

Specifically, to incorporate skeletal representations as a geometric prior, SPEAL comprises three key components: Skeleton Extraction Module (SEM), Skeleton-Aware GeoTRansformer (SAGTR), and Correspondence Dual-Sampler (CDS). First, building on insights from the medial axis transform (MAT) [7], SEM extracts a set of skeleton points with skeletal features from input point clouds in an unsupervised manner, and is robust to noise and density variances. Next, SAGTR is designed to learn skeleton-aware discriminative features that facilitate accurate and robust correspondences. It explicitly captures the topological natures and effectively learns inter-point-cloud geometric correlations with our skeletal representations. Finally, CDS samples reliable correspondences from both superpoints and skeleton points, producing reliable coarse correspondences with awareness of the skeletal structure.

Extensive experiments are carried out on two datasets. One is KITTI Odometry, a large-scale outdoor registration benchmark [8], together with its cross-source variant KITTI CrossSource, which we propose. The other is a large-scale cross-source dataset consisting mostly of unstructured forest scenes [9]. The results demonstrate that SPEAL is effective and robust for both same-source and cross-source point cloud registration, as well as for point clouds of unstructured scenes.

Overall, our contributions are threefold:

- • We propose a novel learning-based point cloud registration approach, SPEAL, which is the first to use skeletal representations as a geometric prior to achieve improved performance.

- • The proposed SEM is an effective and portable skeleton extractor. Our SAGTR combined with CDS produces accurate and robust correspondences for both same-source and cross-source point cloud registration.

- • KITTI CrossSource, a novel cross-source point cloud dataset, meets the dire need [10] for cross-source point cloud registration benchmarks, opening up the possibility to bridge the gap between sensor technology and cross-source applications.
